2608.27176.title: When Text Misleads: Inconsistent-Aware Reasoning for Audio-Grounded Dialogue
2608.27176.paper_summary: Understanding spoken dialogue requires joint reasoning over lexical content and paralinguistic acoustic signals such as emotion and conversational intent. However, existing evaluations often allow shortcuts based on transcripts or single-modality solutions, obscuring whether models genuinely ground predictions in speech. We formalize this failure mode as cross-modal disagreement, where transcripts suggest plausible but incorrect surface interpretations while acoustic cues such as prosody or speaking style support different answers. We develop a scalable framework that identifies text-biased surface interpretations and converts disagreement regions into conflict QA examples. We also include consistent cases where transcript-based and speech-grounded interpretations agree, enabling evaluation beyond adversarial audio dependence. This results in ContraTalk, a controlled benchmark containing 501 questions across five discourse dimensions: interaction behavior, emotion state, dialogue act, social stance, and conversational intent. We further develop an agentic-style reasoning framework that converts speech into an Audio Twin, a text-readable representation of localized acoustic cues that exposes acoustic evidence to the reasoning model. Experiments show that strong text-only LLMs exceed 90% accuracy in consistent cases but drop to 33-48% in conflict cases. Direct AudioLLMs provide only partial grounding, still selecting the transcript-biased trap in roughly 30-40% of conflict cases. Our Audio Twin framework improves conflict-case accuracy while reducing trap selection, but its consistent-case behavior remains backbone-dependent. These results identify transcript-based shortcuts as an important failure mode in spoken dialogue understanding and show that explicit acoustic evidence aggregation provides a more controllable interface for diagnosing and improving speech-grounded reasoning.
2608.27176.paper_summary_zh: 理解口語對話需要對詞彙內容和副語言聲學信號（如情感和對話意圖）進行聯合推理。<lb/>然而，現有的評估往往基於轉錄文本或單一模態解決方案，讓人無法清楚地判斷模型是否真正將預測根植於語音中。<lb/>我們將這種失敗模式形式化為跨模態不一致，其中轉錄文本暗示了合理但不正確的表面解釋，而聲學線索（如語調或說話風格）則支持不同的答案。<lb/>我們開發了一個可擴展的框架，能夠識別文本偏見的表面解釋，並將不一致區域轉換為衝突問答範例。<lb/>我們還包括了一致的案例，其中基於轉錄的解釋和基於語音的解釋達成一致，從而使評估超越對抗性音頻的依賴。<lb/>這導致了ContraTalk，一個受控基準，包含501個問題，涵蓋五個話語維度：互動行為、情感狀態、對話行為、社會立場和對話意圖。<lb/>我們進一步開發了一個代理風格的推理框架，將語音轉換為音頻雙胞胎，這是一種可讀的文本表示，顯示了局部聲學線索，將聲學證據暴露給推理模型。<lb/>實驗顯示，強大的僅文本大型語言模型在一致案例中超過90%的準確率，但在衝突案例中降至33-48%。<lb/>直接的音頻大型語言模型僅提供部分基礎，仍在大約30-40%的衝突案例中選擇了偏向轉錄的陷阱。<lb/>我們的音頻雙胞胎框架提高了衝突案例的準確性，同時減少了陷阱選擇，但其在一致案例中的表現仍然依賴於基礎模型。<lb/>這些結果確定了基於轉錄的捷徑作為口語對話理解中的一個重要失敗模式，並顯示明確的聲學證據聚合提供了一個更可控的界面，用於診斷和改善基於語音的推理。
